title: #cellinoandbarnes #theatre #comedy #offbroadway #nyc #plays #foryou #...
transcript: do you guys remember Cellino and Barnes the lawyers in the TV commercials with the catchy jingle? cause right now there's an off Broadway play about them but it's a comedy it's basically tells the story of how they met and eventually went their separate ways but just all told in a deeply, deeply unserious way just very silly deliberately cartoonish I saw it last weekend and overall I found it really charming I think my only criticism of it is that I did think it went on maybe just a bit too long or rather that that the bit maybe just got a bit old after a while but I'm glad I saw it it was a fun time overall and I also kind of appreciated what it was doing on a broader level sort of in the same way that an observational comedian will take small experiences from everyday life and put a spotlight on them and there's that fun feeling of like “oh, this is something that like a lot of us are experiencing but no one ever thought to point it out” so it can be kind of validating and even weirdly cathartic and I felt that way with this show where like for all of the people who saw this commercial over and over and heard that jingle a million times the imprint of Cellino & Barnes is undeniable despite being so incredibly trivial to when they sing the jingle for the first time in this show the audience that I was in went absolutely nuts and it was this kind of beautiful shared experience of collectively acknowledging that like it's so stupid that everyone in this room knows this jingle by heart but we do And we can't say that we love it because it's just a dumb commercial but it made itself important to us, against our wills just by its sheer constant presence and I think this show plays on that amusing cognitive dissonance where like even though the way they go about it is so silly they're giving this story like the full origin story treatment that none of us knew we needed
